question: Can you draw a chromosome ideogram for human chr8?

files.eval_guideline: Ideogram must depict chromosome 8 with cytogenetic band coloring per standard Giemsa-stain convention (dark/light/centromere/heterochromatin bands); pixel rendering, fonts, and exact color shades may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files are named ideogram.png and are PNG images, which fits the task of drawing a chr8 ideogram. It is the only candidate file.
files.strategy_reasoning: The output is a PNG image, and the guideline asks about what it shows (chr8 with standard Giemsa band coloring). It also says pixel rendering, fonts and color shades may differ, so a semantic visual check is the right fit.

comparison_details.explanation:
The reference is a plain horizontal ideogram of chr8 with an Mb axis from 1 to about 145. It shows Giemsa bands in white, light gray, dark gray and black, with a red centromere at about 43–47 Mb. The candidate shows the same chromosome on a 0–145 Mb axis using the same Giemsa colours: gneg is white, gpos25/50/75 are graded grays, gpos100 is black and acen is red. It also adds band names, p- and q-arm brackets, rounded ends, a pinched centromere and a legend.

The two band sequences match closely when read in order. On the p arm, both show white, then dark gray (p23.2), a wide white band, black (p22), white, mid gray (p21.2), white, dark gray (p12), small light/white bands and then the centromere at about 43–47 Mb. On the q arm, both show white, mid- and light-gray blocks around 55–70 Mb, then black (q21.11), dark gray, white, black (q21.3), white, light gray (q22.2), white, dark gray (q23.1), black (q23.3), gray (q24.12), white, gray (q24.21), white, dark gray (q24.23) and white at the end.

I estimated band positions in the reference from its tick spacing. Some bands appear shifted by a few Mb, for example the q21 dark blocks. This may come from a different genome build (for example hg19 versus hg38) or from rough rendering, and it does not change the banding pattern. The candidate meets the guideline: it is chromosome 8 with standard Giemsa colouring and a marked centromere. It has no heterochromatin band, which matches the reference because chr8 has no gvar region. The differences are in presentation, plus small possible differences in coordinates.
